step_checks.checker: STANDS. Re-derived by hand. With chi(M) = product of s over the ON links, a ferry M -> M-(v,w)+(w,v') multiplies chi by s(v,w)s(w,v'), which cancels its sign. A four-ring trade toggles all four ring links, so chi(M)chi(M') = sigma_f, and the native -J4 becomes -J4 sigma_f. Round any closed loop each link toggles an even number of times, so the loop sign is the product of sigma over rings traded an odd number of times. On the sodalite net and on the 12/24-site tori each link lies on exactly one geometric square, so with squares only the background alone is sign-blind; with wrapping four-cycles (alpha) it is not. Numerically: 0 violations in 32 runs (8 classes x alpha/beta x with/without six-ring trades). Wording: "signs live only in the trades" holds in the chi gauge; in the native basis they ride on the ferry. "Exactly one kind of loop" is the elementary loop; the general law is the odd-ring product.

STANDS, reproduced exactly with my own Fractions. Ferry -22577/545531250000000 (10 orderings). Blank four-ring -161271/1195529420000 = -3259.48819 |A| (24 orderings; equals the hand formula). Record -57719499/416423383040000 = -3349.19817 |A|. Partner = blank. Six-ring blank/partner -2.41311 |A|, record -2.48960 |A|. Note that every amplitude is NEGATIVE: the native trade is -J4. The seat's code did not keep that sign (correction 1).

THEOREM STANDS; ITS 12-SITE EXAMPLE IS MISLABELLED. The 176-state sector whose "four levels lie within 1.1e-11" is the SIGNED model. At 60 digits it is an exact pair, then another exact pair 2.45e-19 |A| higher. The UNSIGNED 176 sector is single: split 2.2906e-8, pattern 1+2+1 within 4.581e-8. Test: the seat's "signed" ground energy (-6609.731183) lies BELOW its "unsigned" one (-6609.730586). That is impossible if the latter were the all-negative (stoquastic) control. The 24-site labels are swapped the same way.

REFUTED as stated (sign error). Correct sign, 60-digit, all 8 classes. Reading beta: sectors 176/36/36. The SIGNED 176 sector has an EXACTLY two-fold lowest level (two exact pairs 2.45e-19 apart, next level +0.04408); the unsigned one is single (2.2906e-8). The 36-sectors are single (2.000000 signed, 1.999999 unsigned). Reading alpha: one 248 sector, single. Signed split 1.3959e-8 in four classes and 5.973e-9 in the other four; unsigned 7.967e-8. The lowest four levels lie within 2e-8, and the next is +6519 |A|. With six-ring trades both readings are single: beta 2.0729e-2 signed / 2.0730e-2 unsigned; alpha 0.2819 / 2.464 (float). The seat's 4.469e-5 / 2.430e-4 / 2.85e-5 belong to the sign-flipped model; I reproduce them digit for digit with the trades flipped.

REFUTED. The uniform-R pairs reproduce (R = 10: -22.589222167 x2, -22.589221852 x2), but two claims fail. (1) "Only in the uniform-trade variant" is false: an exact sign-made pair is also the lowest level at the native context-dependent sizes (S4). The seat compared correct-sign uniform R with a flipped-sign "true" run, which made the pair seem to vanish. (2) "Nothing protects them" is false. In reading beta the chi-gauged model holds no class information, so all 64 automorphisms of the 12-site torus that fix the partner are symmetries (0 violations). This group is non-abelian; the seat's group is only its 4-element class-preserving subgroup. Randomness symmetric under 4 elements splits the R = 10 pair (3.2e-7 here; the seat found 2.57e-4). Randomness symmetric under all 64 keeps it exact (4e-58), and the same holds at the true sizes.

CONCLUSION STANDS, ONE CLAUSE WRONG. Every symmetry fixes the partner's site. In the chi gauge the 64 elements act as plain permutations (a linear representation), so all 39 involutions square to +1: full turn +1, and any pair is orbital about the partner. Clause (a), "a non-abelian stabilizer is absent (Z2xZ2 on 12 sites, trivial on 24)", holds only in reading alpha. In reading beta the stabilizer has 64 elements on 12 sites and 256 / 512 on 24 sites (partner orbits 1 / 2), all non-abelian, and it is what protects the pair.

QUALITATIVE CAGE STANDS; NUMBERS WRONG. Correct-sign BO, 12 sites, alpha: the lowest manifold is 4 states, all at distance 3, with BO gap 6668.67 |A|. Exact levels relative to the manifold energy: -3.451e-4 |A| signed, -2.000587 |A| unsigned. Beta: projected ferry largest element 1.0 in both (stands). Exact levels -1.044226 |A| signed (the pair) and -1.044823 |A| unsigned. The seat's 4.2e-13 vs 0.896 and -0.0267 vs -1.0111 come from the flipped model, and its beta pair -1.0453 / -1.0447 has the labels swapped.

CONFIRMED in reading beta. With squares only the trade graph is bipartite, so the BO energies do not depend on the trade sign, and the slip does not touch this step. 12 sites: the manifold is 20 states (4 at distance 1, 16 at distance 3) with BO gap 89.71 |A|. 24 sites, partner orbit 1: 20928 states in 7148 trade clusters of at most 32 states; the same 20-state manifold; the best distance-5 position is +3259.49 |A| higher, exactly one blank J4. Partner orbit 2: 8 states, all at distance 3; distance 1 is +179.42 |A| and distance 5 +3349.20 |A|. So at J4/|A| = 3260 the record is bound within three links of its partner by about one J4. Caveats: (i) on 12 sites every A site is within 3 links, so the claim is vacuous there; (ii) "frozen" means bound inside the multiplet with first-order hopping of +-1 |A| (beta), not static; (iii) in alpha the 12-site manifold is 4 states at distance 3; (iv) the binding needs the pinned partner (a modelling step), so whether the bound pair moves as one is untested.
